summary: Formats a float into text using a format string argument and returns the text as a new script string.
reads: argument 1 float; argument 2 format string
writes: nothing (builds a 1024 byte stack buffer and a new script string)
notes: Calls the sprintf-style helper FUN_00551220 and the string maker FUN_004174a0 without reading the printf helper itself. The float is widened to double for the call.

summary: Registers a notification for an object: the script passes an object, a ref, three ints, and the game keeps an entry for it.
reads: this object native; arguments ref, 3 ints; global game singleton via FUN_00419860
writes: notification list of the game resource (inside FUN_0048b500)
notes: Read only the start of FUN_0048b500. If the native instance is missing it writes a Mighty ERROR message into the global error buffer at 0x0062e018 and calls FUN_005513b0. Does nothing when the ref argument is null.

summary: Adds a timer that fires after the given number of seconds, with an int tag.
reads: argument 1 float seconds; argument 2 int; sim time pointer at 0x00617650 (global pointer to a float)
writes: allocates a 0x30 byte timer object and links it into a global timer list
notes: Wake time is the argument plus the current sim time float. The timer keeps a pointer to the owning native object. Constant 0x80000080 is passed as the flags or type. Missing native instance gives a Mighty ERROR message.

summary: Clears bits in the event mask of the object behind this native.
reads: this native; argument 1 int mask
writes: event mask word at offset 0x70 of the object returned by the owner virtual call
notes: Reaches the target through a virtual call (offset 0xc) on the owner at +0xc of the native. Returns nothing but FUN_0048d420 returns the new mask. I did not identify what kind of object holds the mask (input is a guess).

summary: Creates the native side of a game object: finds or creates a native resource instance and links this script object into its list.
reads: this object; arguments GameRef, int, 2 strings; global table at 0x0062f260; global id at object+0xc+0x1d4
writes: links the native record into doubly linked lists, may set a cached id in the owner object at +0x1d4, resizes and attaches the native instance
notes: Did not read FUN_0053a1a0, FUN_0053a2a0, FUN_004290f0, or FUN_00546070. The 4th descriptor argument (a string) is passed on as a pointer. Writes pointers (record addresses) into script-visible structures. Mighty ERROR path if the native is missing.

summary: Registers a callback of the given kind (int argument) for this object, by adding a node to the native instance list.
reads: this native; argument 1 int kind
writes: allocates a 0x1c byte node (kind 8 or 9 seen in the first part) and links it into the native object list; bumps a counter at +0xc4
notes: Only the first part of FUN_00427370 read. The node keeps pointers to the native object. Kind values 8 and 9 are special cased.

summary: Removes a notification that matches the object and an int id.
reads: this native; arguments ref, int
writes: unlinks the matching entry from the game notification list
notes: Calls FUN_0048b670 which looks up the game singleton and walks a list. Only does work when the ref is non-null and the native exists.

summary: Removes every timer that belongs to this object.
reads: this native; global timer list head at 0x006363cc
writes: unlinks matching timer entries from the global list
notes: Read the first 25 lines of FUN_0048b8c0. Missing native instance gives a Mighty ERROR message.

summary: Sets bits in the event mask of the object behind this native.
reads: this native; argument 1 int mask
writes: event mask word at offset 0x70 of the owner object
notes: Mirror of clearEventMask. Does not null check the native instance before the call. The third argument 0 passed to FUN_0048d3d0 is unused.

summary: Unregisters one callback of the given kind for this object.
reads: this native; argument 1 int kind
writes: unlinks the matching node from the native object list
notes: Only the first part of FUN_004274e0 read. Kind 8 is handled first.

summary: Calls an empty callback-removal callee after argument and object helpers.
reads: this native
writes: callee writes nothing; helper effects unread
notes: FUN_004274d0 immediately returns; earlier helpers still need review. See docs/native-lookup.md.

summary: Turns an int into text and returns it as a new script string.
reads: argument 1 int
writes: nothing (builds a 1024 byte stack buffer and a new script string)
notes: Format string is at 0x00613398 (not printed here). Callee FUN_004174a0 read: looks up or creates a script String object keyed by the C string.

summary: Returns a random float: rand() masked to 15 bits (32767 becomes 32766), multiplied by a constant at 0x005f1388.
reads: C runtime rand state
writes: C runtime rand state
notes: Constant at 0x005f1388 not read, likely a tiny scale so the result is under 1.0. Descriptor says F and code returns an x87 float.

summary: Seeds the C runtime random generator from the high resolution timer.
reads: performance counter via FUN_005516c0
writes: C runtime rand seed (srand style call FUN_005d73fb) and timer globals at 0x0076a280 and 0x0076a290
notes: FUN_005516c0 read: calls QueryPerformanceFrequency and QueryPerformanceCounter and writes the results to globals.

summary: Returns the square root of its float argument.
reads: argument 1 float
writes: nothing
notes: Uses the x87 fsqrt on a float10, so the result may differ by rounding from a float sqrtf. No check for negative input.

summary: Wakes one thread waiting on this object.
reads: this object; its waiter list at object+0x14
writes: removes the last waiter from the list (LIFO) and puts it back on the scheduler list via FUN_0041f6f0
notes: Waiters are raw thread pointers in a growable array at object+0x14. Loops from the end skipping null slots. FUN_0041f6f0 read: clears the waiting flag and relinks the thread on a run list; prints an error if the thread is dead or not waiting.

summary: Wakes every thread waiting on this object.
reads: this object; waiter list at object+0x14
writes: empties the waiter list, waking each thread through FUN_0041f6f0
notes: Same data as notify. Pops from the end, so threads wake in reverse order of waiting.

summary: Returns a text description of the object built from a string format at 0x00612d1c and the first field of the object.
reads: this object; field read by FUN_00404ea0 (first field of the object)
writes: new script string
notes: The symbol name of the format is "%s<0x>" style. Passes only one value to the formatter, so the exact output is not confirmed. 256 byte stack buffer.

summary: Makes the current thread wait on this object.
reads: this object; current thread pointer from the argument frame at +4
writes: appends the thread to the waiter array at object+0x14 (creates it on first use); marks the thread waiting via FUN_0041f650 and links it into a wait list
notes: FUN_0041f650 read: errors if the thread is already dead or already waiting, sets flag 0x10. The actual suspending happens in the scheduler, not here.

summary: Returns a copy of the string with one character appended, or with the last character removed when the argument is 8 (backspace).
reads: this string pointer; argument 1 int character code
writes: new script string (256 byte stack copy)
notes: Surprising: append(int) also handles backspace. Characters below 0x20 other than 8 are ignored. Copies exactly 256 bytes from the source pointer, so it reads past short strings.

summary: Returns the length of the string (C strlen).
reads: this string pointer from an int field
writes: nothing
notes: Counts to the terminator, so it returns bytes not characters. Reads the string pointer from the object as a plain int (a 32-bit address in script data).

summary: Returns the Nth token of a string split on a set of delimiter characters.
reads: this string pointer (stored in an int field); argument 1 int index; argument 2 delimiter string
writes: allocates a temporary copy of the text (heap if over 256 bytes, then freed) and a new script string
notes: The script String object holds a raw char pointer in its int field and this reads it as a C string. Uses a strtok style helper FUN_00551200 that takes a save pointer, so it is reentrant. Returns null when there are fewer tokens. Did not read FUN_00551200.

summary: Copies a range of elements from one script array to another, with bounds checks and an overlap safe path.
reads: arguments src array, srcPos, dst array, dstPos, length; array length fields; element value at offset 8 of each element
writes: destination array element values (the int at +8 of each element object)
notes: Decompiled code looks up both arrays with the same call FUN_00403820(DAT_0062dffc), so the real source and destination lookup is likely hidden by the decompiler (treat with care). An index past the array count reads address 8 (null element) and would crash. Negative positions are not checked. Errors: "copy out of bounds" and "empty array" through the global error buffer.

summary: Returns the build number, the constant 606 (0x25e).
reads: nothing
writes: nothing
notes: Constant return.

summary: Compiles all scripts found at a directory path and returns a count or status.
reads: argument 1 string path
writes: script compiler state and files (inside FUN_00418eb0)
notes: Read only the first 40 lines of FUN_00418eb0 (it copies the path and appends a backslash). The compiler builds script class tables that hold pointers.

summary: Returns the real clock time as a float in a scaled unit.
reads: performance counter via FUN_005516c0; constant at 0x005f10a4
writes: timer globals at 0x0076a280 and 0x0076a290
notes: Multiplies the counter result by the constant at 0x005f10a4 (not printed).

summary: Sets the quit flag so the game exits.
reads: nothing
writes: global at 0x0063c520 set to 1
notes: Surprising: the exit(String) version below does not set this flag.

summary: Calls the argument parser and returns without setting the quit flag.
reads: argument 1 string
writes: quit flag unchanged; parser effects unread
notes: FUN_0045d910 has error paths. See docs/native-lookup.md.

summary: Reads the config resource and fills a set of graphics option globals (headlight rays, flares, shadow size and more).
reads: config resource found by FUN_00429190 with key 0x80000000; fields named by strings such as headlight_rays, flares, shadow_size
writes: globals such as 0x006187bc and 0x006187c0
notes: Read the first 40 lines only; the strings suggest more options follow. Prints "Config data not present" through FUN_0054bed0 if the config is missing.

summary: Returns whether the game is loading, read from a global engine object.
reads: int at PTR_DAT_00618d48 + 0x106ed4
writes: nothing
notes: I did not identify what the engine object at 0x00618d48 is (it is large, the field is at offset 0x106ed4).

summary: Resets the loading state: fills 32 ints at 0x00765e8c with the value in 0x00618d6c and stores that value shifted left by 5 at 0x00765f24.
reads: global at 0x00618d6c
writes: 32 ints at 0x00765e8c and an int at 0x00765f24
notes: Callee FUN_005378b0 read in full.

summary: Writes a text line to the game log (stock code).
reads: argument 1 string; the string address plus 0x100
writes: nothing that I could see (FUN_0054bed0 only waits on and releases a semaphore chosen by the int at string+0x100)
notes: Surprising: the decompile of FUN_0054bed0 does not print anything, it only takes and gives a semaphore index read from 0x100 bytes past its argument. That looks like a stripped log or a decompiler error, so what log() really does needs a disassembly check. A null string logs the text "<null>".

summary: Finds or registers a named library or resource pack and returns its slot number, or -1 on failure.
reads: argument 1 string; table at base+0xffe20 (count) and entries 0x70 bytes each
writes: adds the name to the table (copies 0x40 bytes), increments the count at base+0xffe20, may load the pack through FUN_00545fc0
notes: Slot number is shifted left 16 bits to make a resource id. Did not read FUN_00544000, FUN_00544170 or the full FUN_00545fc0. Returns early if the library is already loaded.

summary: Sets the measurement scale: stores the float argument (default 1000) and two values derived from it.
reads: argument 1 float (default 1000.0); constants at 0x005f0ee8 and 0x005e7334
writes: globals 0x0060e04c, 0x0063c770 (arg times constant) and 0x0063c73c (constant divided by arg)
notes: Divides by the argument with no zero check. Likely a unit scale, but I did not follow what reads these globals.

summary: Returns the current simulation time as a float.
reads: float at the address held in PTR_DAT_00617650
writes: nothing
notes: Same sim time pointer that addTimer adds to.

summary: Sets the time of day from a number of seconds and returns the number of whole days.
reads: argument 1 float seconds; constants
writes: global 0x00640988 (seconds in the day, modulo 86400) and flag 0x006178d0
notes: Surprising: descriptor says void but the code returns an int (days = seconds / 86400). Flag 0x006178d0 is 0 when the time is between 01:00 and 05:00 or between 07:00 and 20:00 and 1 otherwise (my reading of the numbers 3600, 18000, 25200, 72000).

summary: Changes the time warp factor and returns the old stored value.
reads: argument 1 float; float at 0x00636448; this pointer; constant at 0x005e73cc
writes: if the argument is at least the constant, sets the warp field at this+0x110 and the base time at this+0x108 (via FUN_004283f0)
notes: The thiscall this pointer is not clearly the object the script passes. The decompiled call passes this as an extra stale value, so the real object is uncertain. Returns the float at 0x00636448 read before the update, not the new one.

summary: Creates the native thread object for a script Thread and stores its address in the script object.
reads: this object; argument 1 string name; thread class data
writes: allocates a 0x38 byte thread record (FUN_0041f340), stores the script object pointer at +0x18 and writes the record address into the script object int field via FUN_0042a9e0
notes: Surprising: a raw 32-bit pointer is stored in a script int field, and the allocation result is not null checked before the +0x18 write. Did not read the rest of FUN_0041f340.

summary: Puts the current thread to sleep for the given seconds.
reads: argument 1 float seconds; performance counter via FUN_005516c0; current thread from this
writes: thread wake time at +0x30 and flag |= 8 at +0x2c
notes: Uses the current thread (this), not an object argument. Returns immediately; the scheduler does the wait.

summary: Starts the script thread: runs its target Runnable once and cleans up if it finishes.
reads: this thread native; field "target" of type java.lang.Runnable; flags at +0x2c
writes: clears flag 2 at +0x2c; calls the target through FUN_00408a30 and, if it ends, marks the thread dead and clears the native pointer in the script object
notes: The test (flags | 2) != 0 is always true in the decompile, so the start guard looks broken or mis-decompiled. Read FUN_00408a30 only (it calls FUN_004207c0 with the owner at +0xc), not the script runner.

summary: Stops the thread: marks it dead and clears the native pointer in the script object.
reads: this thread native
writes: flag 0x80 at +0x2c (after removing from a wait list if flag 0x10 is set), native pointer field set to 0
notes: FUN_0041f780 read in full. Does not free the thread record.

summary: Returns the straight line distance between this Vector3 and another.
reads: this x y z fields and the argument x y z fields, looked up by field name
writes: nothing
notes: Fields are looked up by name strings each call. The two points are not clamped. Result via x87 sqrt.

summary: Returns the length of this Vector3.
reads: this x y z fields
writes: nothing
notes: Plain sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z).

summary: Scales this Vector3 to a fixed length in place, unless its length equals the constant at 0x005e73cc.
reads: this x y z fields; constants at 0x005e73cc and 0x005f08f0
writes: this x y z fields
notes: The constants are probably 0.0 and 1.0 but I did not read them. Compares the float length for exact equality with the first constant.

summary: Rotates this Vector3 by yaw, pitch and roll from the Ypr argument and returns this same object.
reads: this x y z; Ypr argument 3 float fields
writes: this x y z fields (written in place)
notes: Surprising: descriptor says it returns a Vector3 but it returns this after changing it in place. FUN_0054ecd0 read: builds a 3x3 rotation matrix from sin and cos of the three angles. The decompile of the matrix index math is messy (stack layout confused) so I did not confirm which matrix elements multiply which fields.
